title: FloodGuard planning protocol v1b: engineering addendum
status_note: Incomplete draft written by an AI coding agent. Agents draft, humans sign. Nothing in this file is in force. It cannot be signed while any entry in open_items is open, while any parameter named by an open item is empty, or while any entry in drafter_readings awaits confirmation. Until the signed file's SHA-256 is recorded in docs/proposal_execution/RECEIPTS.jsonl, no FPPS, no A-E class and no ensemble may be computed for any real unit. No receipt has been written.
drafted_by: AI coding agent (Claude), on the owner go-ahead R5 of 2026-10-01
purpose: Fix the engineering parameters that the decision rules in v1a need before any score is computed: the routing corridor, the grade-join policy, closure rule v1, the facility sets and the corroboration rule, critical-link selection, the national vulnerability anchors, the ensemble grid, the selection rules for the scenario and engine grid, and the inputs that class rule v2 needs. Plan row G7b.

depends_on.rule: v1b is signed only after v1a's SHA-256 is recorded in RECEIPTS.jsonl. That value is written into v1a_sha256 before v1b is signed. It must equal both the SHA-256 of the committed v1a file and the value in the v1a receipt line; a test and the receipt script check both.
depends_on.exploratory_knowledge_disclosure: The disclosure in v1a applies to this file. Items EK-02, EK-03, EK-04, EK-12, EK-13 and EK-R5 informed parameters set here.

may_run_before_v1b_is_in_force: Closure builds and the regression against the finals closed-edge IDs (E3).
The baseline critical-link ranking, which uses no flood input (E6).
The national dependent-share percentiles, which are constants for all of Thailand and not a score for any unit.
may_not_run_before_v1b_is_in_force: Any FPPS for a real unit.
Any A-E class for a real unit, including would-be classes and v2 classes.
blinding.reading_status: Drafter reading DR-B07. Plan 2.3 item 5 allows 'context, access and closure builds' before v1b. The draft adds two things to that list: the baseline critical-link ranking (E6), which the plan schedules after v1b, and the national dependent-share percentiles, which plan 3.4 says are computed in v1b. It also limits the ban to real units, as in v1a drafter reading DR-A06. The owners confirm or amend the list at signing.
blinding.status_at_drafting: None of the builds above has been run for this protocol. No value in this file comes from a new computation.

context_call.aoi_geometry: Union of the eight Mae Sai tambons TH570901-906, 908 and 909.
context_call.reporting_geometry: Union of the Thai COD-AB ADM3 polygons that intersect the corridor polygon. It is not the eight tambons, because build_context_inputs limits demand, destinations and road segments to the reporting geometry.
context_call.tambon_attribution: Done downstream of the context build.

construction.plus: 3 km buffers along the trunk and primary routes from AOI-02 to three hospitals
construction.distance_note: The three hospitals are 27-33 km from Mae Sai.
construction.road_source: OpenStreetMap Thailand extract already on disk

route_selection_rule.proposal: For each of the three hospitals, take the baseline fastest vehicle path on the national OSM graph from the AOI-02 boundary to the hospital way, keep its trunk and primary segments (including links), buffer them by 3 km and union the result with AOI-02. Record the path edge IDs.
route_selection_rule.why_needed: The plan names the routes as trunk and primary routes to the hospitals but does not say how a route is picked.

corridor_polygon.rejected_alternative: A full 35 km disc (about 8,700 square kilometres): roughly 10-16 times AOI-02's edge count; AOI-06 at about 1,000 square kilometres already cost 16.6 minutes and 4.39 GiB.
corridor_polygon.tolerance: TH570902 and TH570909 have 0.99999 coverage and are treated as full under a declared tolerance of at least 0.999.
corridor_polygon.compute_window: Builds run serially in a declared compute window with no concurrent SNAP jobs.

se2_frame.note: New planning frames live in resources/planning_frames/, not resources/aoi/, so load_aois still returns exactly six AOIs. The SE2 routing geometry and its hospital destinations are not specified in the plan.

grade_join_policy.signed_decision_text: D13: Endpoint-only coincident joins in grade_join.py are logged. The finals contract is unchanged.
rules: A join is made only where the endpoints of two road segments coincide. No join is made at a mid-segment crossing.
Every join is logged with its provenance: the two source way IDs, the node IDs, the coordinate and the rule version.
The 20 reviewed AOI-01 junctions are reused as they are.
The finals contract and the nine SHA-bound finals modules are unchanged. The finals rule that proximity never creates a join still holds for the finals path.
grade_join_policy.module: src/floodguard/grade_join.py (new; does not exist on this lineage)
grade_join_policy.coincidence_tolerance_proposal: 0 m: identical OSM coordinates at 1e-7 degree precision.

closure_rule_v1.geometry: Each edge is the straight segment between its two nodes, projected to EPSG:32647. Intersected length is the length of that segment inside the flood extent. Intersected fraction f is min(1, intersected length / segment length). This is the measurement used in src/floodguard/evidence_flood_scenario.py.
closure_rule_v1.geometry_status: Drafter reading DR-B02. The plan does not say how intersected length is measured or what counts as 'any intersection'. Both are taken from src/floodguard/evidence_flood_scenario.py (straight node-to-node segment in EPSG:32647; an edge is intersected when the length inside the extent is greater than 1e-6 m), so that the permissive regression can match the finals closed-edge IDs exactly. The owners confirm at signing.

central.closed_when: f >= 0.5 OR intersected length >= L(road class); bridges and culverts close at f >= 0.25

permissive.closed_when: any intersection: intersected length > 1e-6 m, the threshold in src/floodguard/evidence_flood_scenario.py that the regression must reproduce
permissive.note: Under this level no intersected edge stays open, so the delay factor has no effect.

closure_rule_v1.delay_factor_pairing_status: Drafter reading DR-B01. Plan 5 item 11 axis 2 lists 'strict / central / permissive, with delay penalty k = 2 / 4 / 6', and plan 5 item 2 states the delay formula only for the central level, with k = 4. The draft pairs k = 2 with strict, 4 with central and 6 with permissive, which gives the plan's 540 cells and 27 routing combinations. The other reading, k as a separate three-level axis, would give 1,620 cells. The owners confirm at signing.

parameters.delay_formula: travel time x (1 + k x f), for edges that are intersected for at least 20 m and are not closed
parameters.raster_minimum_polygon_note: For T2 rasters, polygons under 5 pixels are dropped before intersection.

unassigned_road_classes.proposal: motorway uses the 50 m threshold; residential and unclassified use the 30 m threshold, following the grouping in src/floodguard/road_risk.py ROAD_CLASS_FACTORS.

delay_under_strict.proposal: Under strict, an edge intersected for at least 20 m with f < 0.5 is delayed with k = 2. Under central the plan's wording applies with k = 4.
delay_under_strict.status: proposed. The plan states the delay only for the central level and lists k = 2 / 4 / 6 beside strict / central / permissive.

closure_rule_v1.closure_is_an_assumption: Every output carries closure_basis: modelled_from_<input>. A flood intersection does not prove a road closure.

regression.rule: The permissive level on the AOI-01 finals context reproduces the finals closed-edge IDs exactly.
regression.result_shape: When the regression is run, result is an object: walking_closed_edges, vehicle_closed_edges, closed_edge_ids_match_exactly (true or false) and evidence_sha256 (the SHA-256 of the run output). A failing run is recorded as it is; the file cannot be signed until the match is exact.

closure_rule_v1.field_verification_priority: Segments are ranked by residents affected x disagreement across the strict, central and permissive levels.

hospital.source: OSM hospitals inside the routing context

main_road_entry.definition_proposal: The destination is the nearest node on a trunk or primary edge (including links) inside the routing context.

shelter_location_rule.rule: A coordinate shared by at least 3 rows is flagged location_unverified and those rows are excluded.

facility_sets.pii_rule: The DDPM file has coordinator-name and phone columns. Columns are read through a whitelist, and a test asserts that output keys are a subset of the whitelist.

sets.members: OSM hospitals matched to a DGA health-facility record within 150 m, and DDPM located shelters matched to an OSM building or amenity.
sets.label: corroborated, not confirmed-open
sets.shelter_match_distance_proposal: 150 m, the same as for hospitals.

sets.members: Every OSM hospital in the routing context, main-road entry, and every located DDPM shelter.

facility_sets.identity_rule: Supplied and separately extracted OSM facilities never merge automatically (existing build_context_inputs behaviour).

two_step_access.method: Binary 2SFCA at 15, 30 and 60 minutes on the located DDPM rows.
two_step_access.label: listed planned capacity; scenario

shelters_in_the_ensemble.conflict: The ensemble runs in vehicle mode only (plan 5 item 11). The corroborated and all_listed facility levels add DDPM located shelters, whose access is defined as walking, 30 minutes, and whose data is pitch-level only (plan 3.4, D8b). The plan does not say how a shelter enters a vehicle-only ensemble cell, or what a public overlay may report about cells that use pitch-level data.
shelters_in_the_ensemble.proposal: Inside the ensemble, shelter access is computed by walking at 30 minutes for the shelter service only; hospital and main-road entry stay in vehicle mode. Cells that use DDPM shelters are pitch-level. For a public overlay, class retention is computed over the cells of the public facility set only, and the overlay says so.

rule: Rank baseline vehicle edges by demand-weighted shortest-path-tree flow.
Add graph bridges (Tarjan) to cover the all-routes-lost case.
Fully reroute only the top 200 ranked edges.
Output the top 20 per case, each with a bridge flag and an in-extent flag.
critical_link_selection.demand_weight: WorldPop 2020 residents at each origin node.
critical_link_selection.selection_details_status: Drafter reading DR-B03. The plan says 'demand-weighted SPT flow' and names no demand layer and no tie-break. The draft uses WorldPop 2020 residents at each origin node and breaks ties on stable edge ID, following src/floodguard/evidence_interventions.py. The owners confirm at signing.
critical_link_selection.destination_set_proposal: The public facility set (OSM hospitals and main-road entry), vehicle mode, so the ranking does not depend on DDPM data.
critical_link_selection.no_example_figure: No example figure is quoted before the run.
critical_link_selection.reuse: Ranking pattern of src/floodguard/evidence_interventions.py select_interventions (stable IDs break ties; no scenario outcome tunes the selection).
critical_link_selection.desk_check: An internal single-reviewer desk check (team member R. Ulwani) of the top 20 against imagery, OSM history and news. It is not independent expert review.

binding_options.bound_here: E6 is run before signing; path and sha256 above are filled in.
binding_options.bound_in_first_run_receipt: v1b is signed with the rule alone; the ranking's SHA-256 is recorded in the receipt of the first run, before any scoring.

national_vulnerability_anchors.definition: Percentiles, across Thai tambons, of the dependent share: residents aged 0-14 plus residents aged 60 and over, divided by all residents, from the WorldPop 2024 1 km age counts.
national_vulnerability_anchors.computed: Once, in v1b, before any case scoring. The values are constants for every case and lane.

uses.P10_P90: Default anchors of the vulnerability component (v1a scoring_frame).
uses.P75: Class rule v2 trigger A (dependent-share concentration).

age_rasters.product: WorldPop Global2 R2025A v1, Thailand, 2024, constrained total-sex age counts, 30 arc-second (about 1 km), 1km_ua
age_rasters.rights: Public catalog says CC BY 4.0. Public derivatives require purpose-specific review.

tambon_boundaries.product: HDX Thailand COD-AB, layer tha_admin3 (valid on 2022-01-22)

method.allocation: Each 1 km cell's counts are allocated to a tambon by the projected-area fraction of the cell inside the tambon, as in scripts/bridge_worldpop_age_access.py.
method.allocation_status: Drafter reading DR-B04. The plan does not say how 1 km cells are assigned to tambons. The draft follows scripts/bridge_worldpop_age_access.py (projected-area fraction). The owners confirm at signing.
method.unit_set_proposal: Every tha_admin3 unit in Thailand with at least 100 modelled 2024 residents (the minimum-denominator rule). The number of units used and the number excluded are recorded.
method.percentile_method_proposal: Unweighted across tambons, linear interpolation between order statistics.
method.module: src/floodguard/normalisation.py (new; does not exist on this lineage)

national_vulnerability_anchors.caveat: Modelled 1 km age composition; not observed. Mixed vintages are disclosed: 2020 demand, 2024 age, 2022 boundaries, 2026 OSM.

ensemble_grid.runs: Full-chain reruns, vehicle mode. Walking is excluded from the ensemble because the walking access gap is 46-100 with no flood.

core_axes.t2_lane_levels: M1-v2: Kittler-Illingworth threshold -1 / 0 / +1 dB. Legacy mask on AOI-01 only: 1.5 / 2.25 / 3.0 dB.

one_pixel_m.note: Plan 5 item 11 gives 20 m only for the minus level ('-1 px / 20 m erosion'). It gives no distance for the plus level and none for vector agency products, which have no pixel. Confidence condition C4 in v1a uses the same two levels.
one_pixel_m.proposal: 20 m for the minus and the plus level and for every input, raster or vector. For a vector product the level is a 20 m negative or positive buffer in EPSG:32647.

core_axes.t2_levels_note: The plan defines the T2 levels for M1-v2 and the legacy mask only. M1-literal, the UN-SPIDER reproduction and the A6-prime classifier are also flood inputs of case O1. The A6-prime classifier outputs a probability, and the plan gives no threshold that turns it into an extent (plan 4.2 A5 says only 'A6-prime thresholded').

t2_levels_proposal.UN-SPIDER reproduction: minus / as-provided / plus one pixel on the output extent; the ratio 1.25 is not tuned
t2_levels_proposal.a6_prime_extent_threshold: 0.5 on the isotonic-calibrated probability, fixed on GEOID development tiles before any Mae Sai run

core_axes.levels_status: The pairing of k with the three levels is drafter reading DR-B01.

core_axes.rescale_formula_proposal: Within each 1 km cell of the WorldPop 2024 grid, multiply every 2020 100 m count by the ratio of the cell's 2024 total (the sum of the 20 age bands) to the sum of the 2020 100 m counts inside the cell. A cell whose 2020 sum is zero keeps zero, and the 2024 residents it leaves out are reported as unallocated.
core_axes.rescale_formula_status: proposed, not in the plan. The plan says only 'population vintage axis via 2024/2020 1 km rescale'.

ensemble_grid.routing_combinations_note: Only the 3 x 3 x 3 combinations of flood state, passability and facilities need full access runs.
one_at_a_time: Terrain / remoteness proxy in place of the age-based vulnerability, case O1 only.
ensemble_grid.one_at_a_time_status: Drafter reading DR-B05. Plan 5 item 11 lists the terrain proxy under axis 4, beside the two anchor levels, but the 540-cell count (3 x 3 x 3 x 2 x 2 x 5) leaves no room for it as a core level. The draft runs it one at a time, on O1 only. The owners confirm at signing.

terrain_remoteness_proxy.note: The proxy is an ensemble level and the S8 cell, and the plan gives it no definition and no anchor.
terrain_remoteness_proxy.proposal: The definition already in src/floodguard/mae_sai_context.py: a WorldPop cell is proxy-vulnerable when its sampled slope is at least 8 degrees or its nearest drivable OSM road is at least 750 m away. Component value: 100 x clip(proxy-vulnerable share of the unit's residents / anchor, 0, 1). No anchor is proposed: the replay used 0.25 with its results in view (v1a disclosure items EK-R1 and EK-R5), so the owners choose it.

per_tambon_outputs: Median and range of people losing 30-minute access.
Median and range of EED and EER.
Percent of runs keeping the class.
The axis with the largest swing.

headline_rule.fallback_text: no class met the stability rule; shown as unstable: verify
headline_rule.reference_cell_proposal: Retention is the share of the 540 core cells whose v1 class equals the class of the default cell: as-provided flood state, central passability, public facilities, WorldPop 2020, P10 / P90 anchors, default weights.

ensemble_grid.confidence_rule_independence: Confidence rule v1 uses no ensemble output.

declared_cuts.cut_line_6: Population-vintage and vulnerability-anchor axes (540 to 135 cells).
declared_cuts.cut_line_8: Corroborated facility level (public and all-listed stay).

ensemble_grid.reporting: All cells of every lane are reported.

scenario_engine_grid.labels: Scenario cells are SCN (or SCN-ENV when the base is SE1). Engine cells are ENG. Neither is ever counted as observed.
scenario_engine_grid.selection_principle: Links, nodes and facilities are picked by a rule that uses baseline information only. No cell is picked by its outcome, and every cell is reported.

cells.perturbation: Flood-state axis: minus / as-provided / plus one pixel.
Fail the top 3 pre-ranked critical links per tambon.
cells.selection_rule: The three highest-ranked links of the baseline critical-link ranking whose edge lies in the tambon. An edge that crosses a tambon boundary belongs to the tambon that holds its midpoint. Ties break on stable edge ID.
cells.selection_rule_status: Drafter reading DR-B06. The plan says 'the top-3 pre-ranked critical links per tambon' and does not say how a link is assigned to a tambon. The draft assigns it by where the edge lies, and by the midpoint for an edge that crosses a boundary. The owners confirm at signing.

cells.perturbation: Fail the top-k bridge edges only (OSM bridge=yes on the shortest-path-tree union).
cells.selection_rule: The k highest-ranked bridge edges of the baseline ranking.
The facility is named in the plan. Its OSM ID is recorded from the E4 context.

cells.perturbation: A temporary shelter at the predeclared add_destination node in each A or B tambon.
cells.selection_rule: The add_destination rule of src/floodguard/evidence_interventions.py: the demand node ranked first by residents without 30-minute access, then finite baseline person-minutes, resident count and stable node ID. The node is determined per tambon from the baseline context before scoring; which tambons receive the cell is decided by their SE1 class after scoring.

binding_options.bound_here: The per-tambon node list is built from the E4 context before signing; path and sha256 are filled in.
binding_options.bound_in_first_run_receipt: v1b is signed with the rule alone; the node list's SHA-256 is recorded in the receipt of the first run, before any scoring.

cells.class_used_for_selection_proposal: The binding v1 scenario class of the SE1 reference cell. A tambon receives the cell when that class is A or B.
cells.note: Plan 6.3 wants nodes fixed before any scoring, and the plan gives no slot for the node list. The plan says 'each A/B tambon' without saying which class rule or which ensemble cell decides.

cells.perturbation: Age-based vulnerability versus the terrain / remoteness proxy.
cells.note: Drafter reading DR-B08. Plan 6.2 names O2 as the base; plan 3.4 and the signed frame restrict the terrain proxy to O1. This draft follows 3.4. O1 and O2 share the same eight-tambon frame. The owners confirm at signing.

cells.selection_rule: No selection: all three. Pitch level only (D8b).
Not attempted: no return-period layer. Reported as extended target not attempted.
tests/fixtures/sample_population.csv as asserted in tests/test_scoring.py. The five fixture units cover classes A-E, with the fifth forced to E by low confidence.

cells.perturbation: Synthetic rows at the class boundaries.
cells.selection_rule: FPPS exactly 35; exposure / access gap 70 / 70; road criticality / access gap 75 / 55; exposure / access gap 65 / 50; each boundary at +/-0.01; all components 0; all components 100.

cells.perturbation: A minimal perturbation of one real row, labelled synthetic, to show a counterfactual class C.
cells.selection_rule_proposal: Take the O2 unit with the highest exposure component. Raise the single component that is furthest below the class C thresholds to the threshold value, and no other. Label the row synthetic.
cells.note: The plan gives only an example that names a tambon and a value; that example was written with exploratory rows in view (v1a disclosure item EK-04).

cut_lines.5: S5 and S9 (2SFCA at 10 percent only).

class_rule_v2_inputs.note: v1a class_rules.v2 names inputs that depend on v1b. The plan does not define them. Each definition is empty until an owner decides. The proposals are the drafting agent's, and the numbers in them (100 residents, 10 percent) have no data behind them.

trigger_B_isolation.proposal: A top-20 link of the case's baseline critical-link ranking that intersects the flood extent is closed on its own. The trigger fires when at least 500 of the unit's residents who had a baseline vehicle route to a hospital or a main-road entry lose every such route.

trigger_C_serving_facility.proposal: A facility serves a unit when it is the baseline-nearest facility of its kind, by vehicle travel time, for at least 100 of the unit's residents. 'Inside the extent' means the facility point, or the centroid of its footprint, is inside the flood extent. 'Uniquely located' follows facility_sets.shelter_location_rule.

trigger_D_recurrence_flag.proposal: The flag is set when at least 10 percent of the unit's non-permanent-water land has JRC Global Surface Water occurrence of at least 25 percent. If GISTDA Repeated Flood Areas is obtained, the same land-share test is applied to that layer instead.
trigger_D_recurrence_flag.note: The 25 percent occurrence threshold is in v1a. The land share that turns pixels into a unit flag is not in the plan. JRC tiles for parts of the cases are not on disk (downloads DL-1 and DL-2).

rules: While status is incomplete_draft, open items are closed by editing this file. In one edit: fill in every parameter the item lists in parameter_pointers, set the item's status to closed and add its closure (the value, the producing run and its receipt or output SHA-256).
A closed item with an empty parameter is refused by the tests, and a file with status draft_for_signature or signed that has an empty parameter is refused by the schema.
When every open item is closed and every section's status is fixed, the status becomes draft_for_signature, and the signers may amend and sign.

At signing, every entry in drafter_readings is set to confirmed or amended. An amended entry is also listed in signature_block.amendments_at_signing, and the parameter it points to is edited to match.
After the signed file's SHA-256 is recorded in RECEIPTS.jsonl, this file is not edited again.
Any later change needs planning_protocol_v2 with a written reason. Every run is reported.

status_values.incomplete_draft: At least one open item is open. Cannot be signed.
status_values.draft_for_signature: Every open item is closed and every parameter it names is filled in. Not in force.
status_values.signed: Set by the signers in the same edit that fills the signature block. In force only once the SHA-256 of that committed file is in RECEIPTS.jsonl.

receipt.note: This file never records its own SHA-256. Whether it is in force is read from RECEIPTS.jsonl, not from this file.

assumptions: Parameters marked as proposals are the drafting agent's reading of a point the plan leaves unstated; their slots are empty and each is named by an open item. Values that are filled in but do not come from the plan are listed in drafter_readings. Neither kind carries authority until an owner confirms it.
Counts quoted from the plan (shelter rows, closed-edge counts, hospital distances) were verified by the plan's authors, not re-run for this draft.
The on-disk check covers file presence and, for the age rasters, the manifest SHA-256 and byte sizes. Raster contents were not opened.

The open-item list was extended after review from 11 to 18 items. It covers every empty parameter in this file; a test checks that. It cannot show that no further unstated choice remains, and the signers add any they find.

signature_block.note: Not an independent review. The two signers are different people. Each signer fills their own entry; nobody fills an entry for someone else. This file cannot be signed while it is an incomplete draft.
attestations_required: Every open item is closed, every parameter it names is filled in, and I have read each closure.
Every entry in drafter_readings is marked confirmed or amended.
No FPPS, A-E class or ensemble has been computed for a real unit since the plan date (2026-09-26) other than the items in the v1a exploratory-knowledge disclosure.
v1a_sha256 above equals the SHA-256 of the committed v1a file and the value recorded in RECEIPTS.jsonl.
